result.title: Online Active Learning Architecture for Safety-Critical Control Systems
result.summary: The transition of information-centric artificial intelligence to safety-critical applications is impeded by the limitations of conventional offline-training paradigms in open-world environments. This paper presents Control AI, an architecture for Online Active Learning (OAL) inspired by the continuous Prediction-Evaluation-Correction process of biological intelligence. The framework combines the hierarchical representation capacity of deep neural networks with the real-time error-feedback adaptation of adaptive control. A prediction model maps sensory input into a latent manifold, an optional latent model represents transitions in that space, and a reconstruction model maps the latent state back to observable signals. Residuals between predictions and measurements provide the internal learning signal. Spatial and temporal cross-reconstruction architectures prevent OAL from collapsing to a trivial identity mapping, while coupled, dual, and localized variants shorten error-transmission paths. Localized predictive coding style OAL is implemented through guidance-backpropagation and target-backpropagation architectures, and hybrid and scaled variants support high-dimensional deployment. The paper focuses on the architectural rationale and the progression from a conceptual feedback loop to practical large-scale configurations.

AI.brief_summary: 提出名为 Control AI 的在线主动学习架构：预测模型把传感输入映射到 latent manifold，可选的 latent 转移模型刻画该空间中的状态演化，重构模型再映射回可观测信号，预测与测量之间的残差作为内部学习信号，并用时空交叉重构与局部化预测编码变体避免退化为恒等映射。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽属安全攸关控制而非多模态推理，其「交叉重构防止表征坍缩」与局部化预测编码的误差传导设计，可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态的训练监督与信息坍缩问题。
